dc.identifier.next_section.value: 34.Qualifications for appointment as Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, or other Members.

dc.identifier.section_page_note.value:
(1) The Appellate Board shall consist of a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, and such other Members as the Central Government may deem fit and, subject to the other provisions of this Act, the jurisdiction, powers and authority of the Appellate Board may be exercised by a Bench thereof.
(2) Subject to the other provisions of this Act, a Bench shall consist of one Judicial Member and one Technical Member and shall sit at such place as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, specify.
(3) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (2), the Chairperson--
(a) may, in addition to discharging the functions of the Judicial Member or Technical Member of the Bench to which he is appointed, discharge the function of the Judicial Member or, as the case may be, the Technical Member, of any other Bench;
(b) may transfer a Member from one Bench to another Bench;
(c) may authorise Vice-Chairperson, the Judicial Member or the Technical Member appointed to one Bench to discharge also the functions of the Judicial Member or the Technical Member, as the case may be, of another Bench.
(4) Where any Benches are constituted, the Central Government may, from time to time, by notification, make provisions as to the distribution of the business of the Appellate Board amongst the Benches and specify the matters which may be dealt by each Bench.
Explanation.-- For the removal of doubts, it is hereby declared that the expression "matter" includes an application or appeal under section 40 or section 42.
(5) If the Members of a Bench differ in opinion on any point, they shall state the point or points on which they differ, and make a reference to the Chairperson who shall either hear the point or points himself or refer the case for hearing on such point or points by one or more of the other Members and such point or points shall be decided according to the opinion of the majority of the Members who have heard the case including those who first heard it.

Summary of the Prisoners Act, 1900

Key Provisions
1.	Examination of Prisoners:
•	A police officer may, with the approval of a Magistrate, arrange for the medical examination of a prisoner when it is likely to provide evidence relating to the commission of an offence.
•	Such examinations must be conducted by a registered medical practitioner.
2.	Transfer of Prisoners (Sections 5–9):
•	The Act authorizes the transfer of prisoners from one prison to another under specified circumstances, such as security, administrative convenience, or legal requirements.
•	Transfers are carried out under lawful orders of the competent authority.
3.	Production of Prisoners in Court:
•	The Act enables prisoners to be produced before courts or other lawful authorities when required for trials, inquiries, or other legal proceedings, subject to prescribed procedures.
4.	Custody During Transit:
•	It provides for the lawful custody and escort of prisoners while they are being transferred or produced before courts.
5.	Duties of Prison Authorities:
•	Prison officers are required to comply with lawful warrants and orders relating to the custody, examination, transfer, and production of prisoners.

dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 
The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (Act No. 37 of 2020) – Brief Summary
The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions (OSHWC) Code, 2020 consolidates and amends laws relating to the occupational safety, health, and working conditions of employees in India. It replaces 13 Central labour laws, including the Factories Act, 1948, the Mines Act, 1952, and the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970, creating a unified framework for workplace safety and labour welfare. The Code was enacted on 28 September 2020 and came into force on 21 November 2025. 
Objectives
•	To consolidate 13 labour laws into a single comprehensive code. 
•	To ensure safe, healthy, and humane working conditions for employees. 
•	To simplify labour law compliance and promote ease of doing business. 
•	To improve welfare and protection of workers across different sectors. 
Key Provisions
•	Introduces single registration for eligible establishments and common licensing for contractors, including all-India licences in specified cases. 
•	Specifies the duties of employers to provide a safe working environment, health measures, welfare facilities, and necessary protective equipment. 
•	Provides for working hours, annual leave with wages, welfare facilities, and occupational safety standards. 
•	Covers provisions relating to contract labour, inter-State migrant workers, mines, factories, plantations, construction workers, beedi and cigar workers, and audio-visual workers. 
•	Allows employment of women in all establishments, including night shifts, subject to prescribed conditions relating to safety, consent, and welfare. 
•	Empowers Inspector-cum-Facilitators to conduct inspections and assist establishments in ensuring compliance. 
•	Prescribes penalties for violations of safety, health, and welfare requirements. 
Significance
•	Replaces multiple overlapping labour laws with a single, simplified legal framework. 
•	Strengthens workplace health, safety, and welfare standards across industries. 
•	Reduces regulatory complexity through streamlined registration, licensing, and compliance procedures. 
•	Balances worker protection with improved ease of doing business, contributing to a more efficient and transparent labour regulatory system
